# Symfony Froala Editor [GitHub](https://github.com/froala/KMSFroalaEditorBundle "Symfony WYSIWYG GitHub") ## Symfony 3 & 4 update This bundle is now compatible with Symfony 2, 3 and 4 on the same branch (dev-master). ## Installation #### Step 1 : Add KMSFroalaEditorBundle to your composer.json (according to your needed version) ``` { "require": { "kms/froala-editor-bundle": "dev-master" } } ``` #### Step 2 : Add the bundle to your bundles.php ``` // config/bundles.php return [ //.. //.. KMS\FroalaEditorBundle\KMSFroalaEditorBundle::class => ['all' => true], ]; ``` #### Step 3 : Import routes ``` // config/routes.yaml kms_froala_editor: resource: "@KMSFroalaEditorBundle/Resources/config/routing.yml" prefix: /froalaeditor ``` #### Step 4 : Install the bundle `$ composer update` #### Step 5 : Configure the bundle **Required settings:** Open `config/packages/config.yaml` and add the following code to set a language: ``` kms_froala_editor: language: "nl" ``` If `config.yaml`doesn't exist you need to create it. **Other Options:** You can use all the available Froala options, refer to the [Options Documentation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) for more information. - For options that require an array, provide a value array. - For options that require an object, provide a key/value array. If you don't add an option on the config file Froala the default values The following example shows each option type: ``` // config/packages/config.yaml kms_froala_editor: toolbarInline: true tableColors: [ "#FFFFFF", "#FF0000" ] saveParams: { "id" : "myEditorField" } ``` **Note:** Some options require plugins, refer to the [Options Documentation](https://editor.froala.com/options/). for more information There are custom options that provide a better integration with Symfony. The following section describes the available custom options: - Use a Froala license number `serialNumber: "XXXX-XXXX-XXXX"` - Disable JQuery inclusion. `includeJQuery: false` - Disable CodeMirror inclusion. `includeCodeMirror: false` - Disable Font Awesome inclusion. `includeFontAwesome: false` - Disable all bundle javascripts inclusion (not concerning JQuery nor CodeMirror). When you are using Grunt or other and you want to include yourself all scripts. `includeJS: false` - Disable all bundle CSS inclusion (not concerning Font Awesome nor CodeMirror). When you are using Grunt or other and you want to include yourself all stylesheets. `includeCSS: false` - Change the froala base path. `basePath: "/my/custom/path"` - Custom JS file. Used to add custom plugins/buttons `customJS: "/custom/js/path"` #### Step 6 : Add Froala to your form The following example shows how to add a froala type in your form: ``` use KMS\FroalaEditorBundle\Form\Type\FroalaEditorType; // Symfony 4 //.. $builder->add( "yourField", "froala" ); // Symfony 2 $builder->add( "yourField", FroalaEditorType::class ); // Symfony 3 & 4 ``` You can override all configuration items: ``` $builder->add( "yourField", "froala", array( "language" => "fr", "toolbarInline" => true, "tableColors" => [ "#FFFFFF", "#FF0000" ], "saveParams" => [ "id" => "myEditorField" ] )); ``` #### Step 7 : Display editor content **Manually:** To preserve the look of the edited HTML outside of the editor you have to include the following CSS files: ``` ``` Also, you should make sure that you put the edited content inside an element that has the class fr-view: ```
{{ myContentHtml | raw }}
``` **Using the Twig extension:** To use the Twig extension, you have to enable the PHP templating engine: ``` // app/config.yml framework: templating: engines: ['twig', 'php'] ``` Next, call the display function (note that the front CSS file is not included if the parameter `includeCSS` is false ): ``` {{ froala_display( myContentHtml ) }} ``` ## More configuration #### Plugins All [Froala plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/) are available. The following example shows how to disable unwanted plugins ``` // app/config.yml kms_froala_editor: pluginsDisabled: [ "save", "fullscreen" ] ``` The following example show how to enable plugins: ``` // app/config.yml kms_froala_editor: pluginsEnabled: [ "image", "file" ] ``` Plugins can be enabled/disabled for each Froala instance by passing the same array in the form builer. #### Concept: Image upload/manager This bundle provides integration with the [Froala image upload functionality](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/image/upload/) to store your images on your own web server (see custom options for configuration like upload folder). If you want to use your own uploader, you can override the configuration. There are custom options that provide a better integration with Symfony. The following section describes the available custom options: - The image upload folder in your /web directory. The default value is: "/upload". `imageUploadFolder: "/my/upload/folder"` - The image upload URL base. Used when you employ URL rewritting for your assets. The default value is the same value as the one provided as folder. `imageUploadPath: "/my/upload/path"` #### Concept: File upload This bundle provides integration with the [Froala file upload functionality](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/file/upload/) to store your files on your own web server (see custom options for configuration like upload folder). If you want to use your own uploader, you can override the configuration. There are custom options that provide a better integration with Symfony. The following section describes the available custom options: - The file upload folder in your /web directory.The default value is: "/upload". `fileUploadFolder: "/my/upload/folder"` - The file upload URL base. Used when you employ URL rewritting for your assets. The default value is the same value as the one provided as folder. `fileUploadPath:"/my/upload/path"` - Your public directory, from the root directory.The default value is: "/web" `publicDir: "/public"` #### Concept: Autosave You can use the Froala autosave functionality to automatically request a save action on your server. The following example shows how to configure its options: ``` // app/config.yml kms_froala_editor: saveURL: "my_save_route" saveInterval: 2500 saveParam: "content" ``` There are custom options that provide a better integration with Symfony. The following section describes the available custom options: - Add some parameters to your save URL. Used when you need parameters to generate your save action route. The default value is: `null`. `saveURLParams: { "id" : "myId" }` You can add some parameters in your save route (see custom options). ## Additional Resources - [Building a Support System Using Laravel PHP Framework and Froala Rich Text Editor – Part 1](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/building-a-support-system-using-laravel-php-framework-and-froala-rich-text-editor-part-1/) - [Froala Image Management in Laravel: Easy for HTML Code Writers](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/simplify-froala-image-management-in-laravel-using-froala-html-code-writer/) - [Building a Support System with Laravel PHP and Froala HTML Editor Sofware – part 3](https://froala.com/blog/editor/tutorials/building-laravel-support-system-part-3-froala-html-editor-software/) _Do you think we can improve this article? ### aiAssist.requestAnswer (params, signal)

Returns: Promise<Object>

Sends a single buffered request to the configured AI backend and resolves with `{ answer, session_id?, webSearchUsed? }`. As of 5.4.0, `params` accepts five additional optional fields, and existing callers that omit them see unchanged behavior. As of 5.5.0, `params` accept `regenerate` (Boolean). When it's `true`, it's passed to `aiAssistRequest` as `data.regenerate`, or sent in the `aiAssistEndpoint` request body, so a caching backend returns a new answer for the same prompt.

-   **params**
    
    Type: Object
    
    The request payload, including the existing `prompt` field plus the optional `webSearchEnabled` (Boolean), `model` (String), `reasoningEnabled` (Boolean), `files` (Array), `referenceUrls` (Array of Strings) fields, and `regenerate` (Boolean).
    
-   **signal**
    
    Type: AbortSignal
    
    Used to cancel an in-flight request.
    

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor');

const answer = await editor.aiAssist.requestAnswer({
  prompt: 'Write a tagline for a coffee shop',
  webSearchEnabled: true,
  model: 'gpt-4o',
  referenceUrls: ['https://example.com/article'],
  regenerate: true
});
```

### aiAssist.requestAnswerStream (params, onChunk, signal)

Returns: Promise<Object>

Streaming sibling of `requestAnswer`, takes the same `params` shape (including the five new fields above) plus an `onChunk` callback that receives raw text deltas as they arrive.

-   **params**
    
    Type: Object
    
    Same shape as `requestAnswer`'s params.
    
-   **onChunk**
    
    Type: Function
    
    Called with each decoded text chunk as it streams in.
    
-   **signal**
    
    Type: AbortSignal
    
    Used to cancel an in-flight request.
    

**Returns:** `Promise<{ answer: string, session_id?: string, webSearchUsed?: boolean }>` — same shape and same rules as `requestAnswer`'s return value above; note that the built-in `aiAssistEndpoint` path only reports `session_id`/`webSearchUsed` for `requestAnswer`, not for the streaming path — only a custom `aiAssistRequest` handler can report them while streaming.

**Note:** A custom `aiAssistRequest` handler that wants to support AI Chat streaming needs to accept and call an optional 3rd argument, `onChunk` — beyond the existing 2-argument contract `requestAnswer` uses. Existing non-streaming integrations are unaffected.

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
var editor = new FroalaEditor('.selector', {}, function () {
  // Call the method inside the initialized event.
  editor.aiAssist.requestAnswerStream(
    { prompt: 'Write a paragraph about the ocean' },
    (chunk) => { console.log('chunk:', chunk); },
    signal
  );
})
```

### aiAssist.showPromptPopup ()

Returns:

Opens the AI Assist prompt popup, allowing users to enter custom prompts for AI content generation.

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
var editor = new FroalaEditor('.selector', {}, function () {
  // Call the method inside the initialized event.
  editor.aiAssist.showPromptPopup();
})
```

### aiChatAssistant.addContextSource (source)

Returns: Object | Promise<Object>

Adds a context source to the active conversation and returns the resolved context source descriptor. File and URL sources are read and resolved asynchronously, so the return value can be a promise that must be awaited before the source id is available.

-   **source**
    
    Type: Object
    
    A descriptor of the shape `{ type: 'document' | 'file' | 'url', file?: File, url?: string }`. The `'selection'` type cannot be added manually, since it appears automatically as a chip whenever the editor has an active selection.
    

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
var editor = new FroalaEditor('.selector', {}, function () {
  // Call the method inside the initialized event.
  editor.aiChatAssistant.addContextSource ({ type: 'url', url: 'https://example.com' });
})
```

### aiChatAssistant.getChatHistory ()

Returns: Array

Returns the complete AI Chat conversation so far, oldest turn first, as plain serializable records. The result is a snapshot rather than a live view, so mutating it has no effect on the panel, and an empty array is returned when there are no messages yet. Each record exposes `id`, `role`, `text`, `createdAt`, `contextText`, `contextKind`, `webSearchUsed`, `applied`, `error`, and `streaming`.

Field

Type

Description

**id**

String

Stable per-message id, also the transcript element's `data-id`.

**role**

'user' | 'assistant'

Who produced the turn.

**text**

String

The message text. For an assistant turn this is the provider's answer as received, before the panel's own fence-stripping and sanitizing for display.

**createdAt**

Number | null

`Date.now()` at the moment the turn was created.

**contextText**

String

What the turn was grounded in, meaning the resolved context sent with the request (document or selection HTML, file text, reference URLs, or the previous response's preview). Empty string when the turn had no context.

**contextKind**

'document' | 'selection' | null

Which in-document source the context came from, or `null` for a chat-only turn or one grounded only in a file or URL.

**webSearchUsed**

Boolean

Whether the backend confirmed it used web search for this answer.

**applied**

Boolean

Whether this answer has been applied to the document.

**error**

Boolean

Whether the turn failed, which renders as the inline error bubble.

**streaming**

Boolean

Whether the answer is still streaming in.

Note: the returned records deliberately do not expose the message's internal `contextRange`, which is a live DOM Range into the editor's own content and is neither serializable nor safe to hand out.

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
var editor = new FroalaEditor('.selector', {}, function () {
  // Call the method inside the initialized event.
  const history = editor.aiChatAssistant.getChatHistory();
  // [
  //   { id: 'fr-ai-chat-msg-1', role: 'user',      text: 'Summarize chapter 2', … },
  //   { id: 'fr-ai-chat-msg-2', role: 'assistant', text: '<p>Chapter 2 argues…</p>', … }
  // ]
})
```

### aiImproveWriting.applyExternalRewriteDirect (range, originalText, answer)

Returns: Boolean

Applies an externally-generated rewrite (e.g. from AI Chat's "Apply to document") using the same word-diff/review logic as Improve Writing itself, for a caller whose own UI already served as the review/confirmation step. When collaborating, it applies the change immediately instead of opening a review popup, a direct edit in "editing" mode, or a tracked suggestion per hunk in "suggesting" mode. This is the only public entry point for applying an externally-sourced rewrite.

-   **range**
    
    Type: Range
    
    A live DOM Range pointing at the exact region of the editor's content that `answer` is meant to replace. This is not something you construct from scratch, it should be the same Range you captured before sending the request to your AI backend (e.g. `editor.selection.get().getRangeAt(0)` for the user's current selection, or a Range spanning the whole editable body when no selection was active). The method re-reads this Range's live text at call time and compares it against `originalText`: if the document changed underneath it in the meantime (the user kept typing while the AI request was in flight), the call fails safely (see Returns above) instead of corrupting unrelated content.
    
-   **originalText**
    
    Type: String
    
    The plain text that `range` contained at the moment you sent the request, a snapshot, not a live read. Pass whatever you read from the editor right before calling your AI backend (e.g. `editor.html.getSelected()`/`range.toString()`), unmodified. The method uses this both to validate the range hasn't gone stale (see above) and as the "before" side of the word-level diff shown to reviewers.
    
-   **answer**
    
    Type: String
    
    The candidate/rewritten text returned by the AI backend, the "after" side of the diff. Plain text or lightly-marked text is expected; any HTML/fencing wrapping the model may have added is stripped internally before diffing.
    

**Returns:**

-   `true`: the rewrite was applied (directly, or as a review flow was started/a tracked suggestion inserted, depending on collaboration mode).
-   `false`:no-op. Either the caller was busy (an Improve Writing session, a collab review, or another AI request was already active), or `range`'s current live text no longer equals `originalText` (the document changed since it was captured) — in both cases nothing is applied, so it's safe to show your own "please try again" message.

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor');

async function rewriteSelectionWithAI(prompt) {
  // 1. Capture the Range and its text BEFORE the async AI call — this is
  //    exactly the pair applyExternalRewriteDirect will validate against.
  const range = editor.selection.get().getRangeAt(0);
  const originalText = range.toString();

  // 2. Send the request to your configured AI backend (reuses the same
  //    request layer AI Chat/Improve Writing use).
  const { answer } = await editor.aiAssist.requestAnswer({
    prompt: `${prompt}\n\n"""${originalText}"""`
  }, new AbortController().signal);

  // 3. Apply the result back into the document using the *same* range/text
  //    pair captured in step 1 — not a freshly re-read selection, since the
  //    user may have clicked elsewhere while the request was in flight.
  const applied = editor.aiImproveWriting.applyExternalRewriteDirect(
    range,
    originalText,
    answer
  );

  if (!applied) {
    // Busy, or the selection changed while waiting for the response.
    console.warn('Could not apply the rewrite — please try again.');
  }
}
```

### collaborative.setPanelState (state)

Returns: void

Puts the side panel into one of its three states.   editor.collaborative.setPanelState('expanded');
});

### collaborative.updatePanelState(expand)

Returns:

The collaboration plugin displays open and resolved comments and suggestions in a side panel on the right side of the editor. This panel can be expanded or collapsed, and this method controls that state programmatically. Expands the side panel when expand is true, collapses it when false, and toggles it when omitted. Returns nothing.  
  
**Note:** On mobile, expanding opens the full sheet instead of the minimized bar.

-   **expand**
    
    Type: (Boolean | undefined)
    
    -   `true` → expand the panel
        
    -   `false` → collapse the panel (to a strip if cards exist, otherwise fully hidden)

})
```

### toast.show(opts)

Creates and displays a toast notification.  
  
**Parameters:**

-   **opts**
    
    Type: Object
    
    Configuration object. All keys are optional.
    

**opts properties**

Property

Type

Default

Description

`title`

String

—

Short headline text rendered in <span class="fr-toast\_\_title">. Automatically HTML-escaped.

`description`

String

—

Supporting body text rendered in <span class="fr-toast\_\_description">. Automatically HTML-escaped.

`html`

String

—

Raw HTML string injected as the entire toast body. When provided, title and description are ignored. Not escaped — caller is responsible for sanitizing.

`type`

String

"default"

Visual variant. One of: "default", "success", "error", "warning", "gray". Appends a fr-toast--<type> modifier class.

`size`

String

"default"

Size variant. One of: "default", "small". Appends a fr-toast--<size> modifier class.

`position`

String

"lt-bt"

Screen position code. See Position Codes table below. Falls back to "lt-bt" for unrecognized values.

`showIn`

String | Element

—

CSS selector string or DOM element that acts as the toast container's parent. Defaults to the editor wrapper element (editor.$wp\[0\]), or document.body if the wrapper is unavailable.

`interval`

Number | false

5000

Auto-dismiss delay in milliseconds. Set to false to keep the toast visible until manually dismissed. Set to 0 to dismiss immediately after rendering.

`undoFn`

Function

—

When provided, an Undo button is appended to the toast. Clicking it invokes this callback, then dismisses the toast. Errors thrown by the callback are silently swallowed.

`hideClose`

Boolean

false

When true, the close (×) button is omitted from the toast.

  

**Returns:**

-   `{ hide: Function }` — when `interval` is `false`. Calling `hide()` removes the toast from the DOM immediately.
    
-   `undefined` — for all auto-dismissing toasts.
    

```
// Auto-dismissing toast (disappears after 5 s by default)
editor.toast.show({
  title: 'Comment added',
  type: 'success'
});

// Persistent toast — must be dismissed manually
const handle = editor.toast.show({
  title: 'Connecting…',
  description: 'Waiting for the collaboration server.',
  interval: false
});
// Later, when the connection is established:
handle.hide();

// Toast with undo button
editor.toast.show({
  title: 'Suggestion accepted',
  undoFn: () => editor.collaborative.setMode('suggesting'),
  interval: 8000
});

// Custom HTML body
editor.toast.show({
  html: '<strong>Version saved:</strong> Draft v2',
  type: 'success',
  position: 'ct-bt'
});

// Small warning at the top-right, no close button
editor.toast.show({
  title: 'Read-only mode',
  type: 'warning',
  size: 'small',
  position: 'rt-tp',
  hideClose: true
});
```

**Position Codes**  
  
Toasts are positioned using a two-segment code: <horizontal>-<vertical>.

Segment

Value

Meaning

Horizontal

`rt`

Right edge

Horizontal

`ct`

Horizontal center

Horizontal

`lt`

Left edge

Vertical

`tp`

Top edge

Vertical

`ct`

Vertical center

Vertical

`bt`

Bottom edge

  

**Full position code reference:**

Code

Position

Notes

`rt-tp`

Top-right

Toasts stack downward

`rt-ct`

Middle-right

Toasts stack downward

`rt-bt`

Bottom-right

Toasts stack upward

`ct-tp`

Top-center

Toasts stack downward

`ct-ct`

Screen center

Toasts stack downward

`ct-bt`

Bottom-center

Toasts stack upward

`lt-tp`

Top-left

Toasts stack downward

`lt-ct`

Middle-left

Toasts stack downward

`lt-bt`

Bottom-left (default)

Toasts stack upward

  

When showIn resolves to document.body, the container is position: fixed. For all other parent elements, the container is position: absolute and the parent is set to position: relative if it was previously static.

### helpers.ensureHeadlessFocus ()

Returns: void

In headless mode, focuses the editor if the current selection isn't inside it, so the browser drops a caret into the content. A toolbar click normally does this for you, and in headless mode there's no toolbar. Call it at the start of an action method that reads the selection. Outside headless mode it does nothing.

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
FroalaEditor.PLUGINS.myHighlighter = function (editor) {
  function apply() {
    editor.helpers.ensureHeadlessFocus();
    editor.format.applyStyle('background-color', 'yellow');
  }
  return { apply: apply };
};
```

### helpers.guardHeadlessUI (pluginApi, methodNames)

Returns: Boolean

For plugins that open their own UI outside the popups and modals system. In headless mode it replaces each named method on `pluginApi` with one that does nothing and returns `false`, and returns `true` so you can skip building UI that will never be shown. Outside headless mode it changes nothing and returns `false`.

-   **pluginApi**
    
    Type: Object
    
    The object your plugin returns.
    
-   **methodNames**
    
    Type: String\[\]
    
    The methods to turn off.
    

#### CODE EXAMPLES

Invoke the method inside the rich text editor:

```
FroalaEditor.PLUGINS.myPicker = function (editor) {
  function open() {
    const dialog = document.createElement('dialog');
    dialog.textContent = 'Pick an item';
    document.body.appendChild(dialog);
    dialog.showModal();
  }
  const api = { open: open };
  editor.helpers.guardHeadlessUI(api, ['open']);
  return api;
};
```

pages.markdown:
# Migrating from Froala V3 to Froala V5

Migrating from Froala V3 to V5 is a seamless transition with no breaking changes. Users will enjoy the same familiar editor, now with more powerful features, an enhanced user experience, and improved stability.

Important To use Froala V5 you need a new API key. Please contact support@froala.com to get your new key.

## **Install Version 5**

To find information on the different options for installing Froala Editor, refer to the [Getting Started guide](https://awsstage.froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/)

## Initialization

Version 5 and version 3 both support the same initialization method, **just add your new API key**, and the editor will continue to function as it did before, but with new features available.

The following example shows how to initialize the editor in version 5.

```
new FroalaEditor('.editor', {
  // Pass options.
  optionName: 'Option Value',
  anotherOption:  'Froala Option',
  yetAnotherOne: 100,
  
  // Bind events
  events: {
    eventName: function (param1, param2) {
      // Get editor instance.
      let editor = this;

      // Callback code here

      // Use editor methods.
      editor.method();

    }
  }
})
```

## Plugins

The following plugins are available when you migrate to version 5:

### V5.3.0

[

  

#### Collaborative

Real-time editing, comments, suggestions, and version history.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/collaborative-plugin/ "Collaborative")

### V5.2.0

[

#### Image Filerobot

Modern easy-to-use image editor for advanced transformations.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/filerobot-image-editor-plugin/ "AI Assist")

### V5.1.0

[

  

#### AI Assist

Bring AI directly into your editor.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/ai-assist-plugin/ "AI Assist")

### V5.0.0

[

  

#### Code Snippet

Insert syntax-highlighted code blocks.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-snippet-plugin/ "Code Snippet")[

  

#### Import From Word4

Import a Microsoft Word (.docx) file content to the editor.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/import-from-word-plugin/ "Import From Word")

V4.7.0

[

  

### Anchor

Adds support for named anchors.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/link-to-anchor-plugin/ "Anchor")[

  

### Page Break

Enables users to insert, reposition, and visualize page breaks directly in the editor.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/page-break-plugin/ "Page Break")[

  

### Export to Word

Export the editor’s content to a Microsoft Word (.docx) file.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/export-to-word-plugin/ "Export to Word")

V4.5.2

[

  

### Find and Replace

Quickly locate specific text within the editor and replace it.

](https://froala.com/find-replace-plugin/ "Find and Replace")

V4.3.0

[

### Filestack

Reliable file uploader, quick delivery, seamless web storage integration, and advanced image transformations.

](https://froala.com/filestack-plugin/ "Filestack")

V4.2.0

[

### Word Counter

Display the word count at the bottom bar of the editor.

](https://froala.com/word-counter-plugin/ "Word Counter")

V4.0.0

[

  

### Markdown Support

Format text content in the editor using predefined markdown syntax.

](https://froala.com/markdown-plugin/ "Markdown")[

  

### Track Changes

Track changes like new or deleted content and style and formatting changes.

](https://froala.com/track-changes-plugin/ "Track Changes")

These plugins, except “Track Changes” plugin, are included by default if you are using the froala\_editor.pkgd.js file. Otherwise you should include their corresponding stylesheet and JavaScript files. If you have set the **pluginsEnabled** option you should add the corresponding plugin identifier.

  
Sample code:

```
new FroalaEditor('#froala-editor',  { 
  pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'link', 'exportToWord', 'codeSnippet'],
});
```

[Learn more about how Froala plugins works.](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/)

 

## New Options

In addition to the new plugins’ configurations, the following API options have been added:

V5.5.0

**[headless</a ></strong >](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#headless)**

Runs the editor without its own toolbar, popups, or styling, so you can build your own UI and drive the editor through the API.</span >

**[preserveListMarkerStyle</a ></strong >](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#preserveListMarkerStyle)**

Controls whether bold or italic on a whole list item is stored on the <li> (styling the marker too) or as <strong> and <em> tags inside it.</span >

**[collabConfig.panel.defaultState</a ></strong >](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#collabConfig.panel.defaultState)**

Sets whether the collaborative side panel starts expanded, collapsed, or hidden.</span >

**[aiChatModels</a > </strong >(updated)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatModels)**

Each model’s webSearch and reasoning flags now control the matching AI Chat toggles. An explicit false disables the toggle for that model.</span >

**[aiChatWebSearchEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWebSearchEnabled) </strong >(updated)**

Now a request. The toggle stays off when the selected model declares webSearch: false.</span >

**[aiChatReasoningEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatReasoningEnabled) </strong >(updated)**

Now a request. The toggle stays off when the selected model declares reasoning: false.</span >

**[aiAssistRequest](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistRequest) </strong >(updated)**

The handler receives regenerate: true when the user clicks Try again, so a caching backend can return a fresh answer.</span >

V5.4.0

**[aiChatWebSearchEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWebSearchEnabled)**

Sets whether the web-search toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off.

**[aiChatModels](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatModels)**

Defines the list of selectable AI models shown in the chat panel’s model dropdown.

**[aiChatDefaultModel](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatDefaultModel)**

Sets which model from aiChatModels is preselected when the panel opens.

**[aiChatReasoningEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatReasoningEnabled)**

Sets whether the reasoning toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off.

**[aiChatStreamResponse](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatStreamResponse)**

Determines whether AI Chat answers stream in gradually or appear all at once.

**[aiChatSupportedFileTypes](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatSupportedFileTypes)**

Lists the file extensions users can attach as AI Chat context.

**[aiChatMaxFileSizeMB](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFileSizeMB)**

Sets the maximum size, in MB, allowed for a single attached file.

**[aiChatMaxFiles](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFiles)**

Caps how many files can be attached to one AI Chat conversation.

**[aiChatRequestTimeoutMs](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatRequestTimeoutMs)**

Sets how long, in milliseconds, to wait for an AI Chat response before timing out.

**[aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext)**

Controls whether “Reference URL” context sources are also folded into the outgoing prompt text.

**[aiChatPanelWidth](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelWidth)**

Sets the initial width, in pixels, of the AI Chat panel.

**[aiChatPanelMaxWidth](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelMaxWidth)**

Sets the maximum width, in pixels, the AI Chat panel can be resized to.

**[aiChatWelcomeMessage](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWelcomeMessage)**

Overrides the intro text shown in the AI Chat panel’s empty-state welcome message.

**[aiImproveWritingPrompt](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiImproveWritingPrompt)**

The instruction sent to the AI backend whenever Improve Writing runs.

**[selectionActionButtons](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#selectionActionButtons)**

Lists the command buttons shown in the popup that appears when text is selected.

**[inlineSuggestions](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestions)**

Enables Gmail-style inline “ghost text” continuation suggestions while typing.

**[inlineSuggestionsDelay](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsDelay)**

Sets the debounce delay, in milliseconds, before an inline suggestion is requested.

**[inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate)**

The prompt template sent to the AI model to generate an inline continuation suggestion.

**[aiSpeechToText](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToText)**

Shows a microphone button letting users dictate their AI prompt instead of typing it.

**[aiSpeechToTextWaveform](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextWaveform)**

Shows an animated “Listening…” waveform in place of the prompt input while recording.

**[aiSpeechToTextListeningText](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextListeningText)**

The label shown next to the recording waveform.

**[aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration)**

Sets the maximum recording duration, in seconds, before transcription is triggered automatically.

**[aiAssistRequest](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistRequest)**

Custom function to handle AI requests, now able to stream via a third onChunk argument and report webSearchUsed on return.

V5.3.0

**[fontSizeCustomMin](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fontSizeCustomMin)**

Defines the minimum font size that can be entered in the Custom Font Size dialog

**[fontSizeCustomMax](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#fontSizeCustomMax)**

Defines the maximum font size that can be entered in the Custom Font Size dialog.

**[importFromWordMammoth](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#importFromWordMammoth)**

Specifies the Mammoth library instance used to import and convert Microsoft Word (.docx) documents into HTML content.

V5.2.0

**[preserveListLineOnBackspace](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#preserveListLineOnBackspace)**

Prevents Backspace from merging or removing a list item when the cursor is at its start.

V5.0.1

[**toolbarButtonsEnabledOnEditorOff**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#toolbarButtonsEnabledOnEditorOff)

Specify which toolbar buttons should remain active even when the Froala editor is disabled.

[**tableHorizontalResizer**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#tableHorizontalResizer)

Control table horizontal resizing.

[**tableVerticalResizer**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#tableVerticalResizer)

Control table vertical resizing.

V5.0.0

[**retainLineBreaksInCellsOnWrap**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#retainLineBreaksInCellsOnWrap)

Control how line breaks within a cell are handled when the cell’s content wraps to multiple lines.

V4.7.2

[**clearFormatOnEnterNewLine**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#clearFormatOnEnterNewLine)

Control whether or not the formatting of the current line is carried over to the new line when you press Enter after pasting content.

[**cleanReduntantStyleOnGet**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#cleanReduntantStyleOnGet)

Removes unnecessary styles from parent elements when retrieving the editor’s content.

V4.6.2

[**proportionalTableResize**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#proportionalTableResize)

Controls how a table behaves when you resize it.

[**enableTableSelection**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#cleanReduntantStyleOnGet)

Enable or disable table selection.

V4.6.0

[**tableDefaultAlign**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#tableDefaultAlign)

Set the default alignment of the table.

[**tableDefaultHeight**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#tableDefaultHeight)

## Why migrate to V5?

Version 5 offers increased stability and reliability, ensuring a smoother editing experience with fewer disruptions. It also includes a range of new features and bug fixes that enhance functionality and address issues present in previous versions. By upgrading, users can take advantage of these improvements while continuing to enjoy the seamless operation of their favorite editor.

Key improvements:

-   Resolved XSS security vulnerabilities.
-   Collaboration features.
-   AI features.
-   Typescript support.
-   Enhanced tables.
-   Improved accessibility.
-   Better iOS mobile support.
-   Enhanced copying and pasting from Word.
-   YouTube Shorts support.
-   Position the toolbar at the bottom on mobile devices.
-   Disable plugins more easily.
-   Filestack integration
-   Headless mode for fully custom editor interfaces.

You can read the [complete changelog here](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/changelog/).

pages.markdown:
# Migrating from Froala V4 to Froala V5

Migrating from Froala V4 to V5 is a straightforward process with no breaking changes, ensuring a seamless transition. Users can quickly and easily upgrade, enjoying the same editor they love while benefiting from more powerful features, an enhanced user experience, and improved stability and reliability. This upgrade promises to maintain the familiar interface while delivering significant enhancements.

Important To use Froala V5 you need a new API key. Please contact support@froala.com to get your new key.

## **Install Version 5**

To find information on the different options for installing Froala Editor, refer to the [Getting Started guide](https://awsstage.froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/overview/)

## Initialization

Version 5 and version 4 both support the same initialization method, **just add your new API key**, and the editor will continue to function as it did before, but with new features available. The following example shows how to initialize the editor in version 5. 

```
new FroalaEditor('.editor', {
  // Pass options.
  optionName: 'Option Value',
  anotherOption:  'Froala Option',
  yetAnotherOne: 100,
  
  // Bind events
  events: {
    eventName: function (param1, param2) {
      // Get editor instance.
      let editor = this;

      // Callback code here

      // Use editor methods.
      editor.method();

    }
  }
})
```

## Plugins

The following plugins are available when you migrate to version 5:

### V5.3.0

[

#### Collaborative

Real-time editing, comments, suggestions, and version history.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/collaborative-plugin/ "AI Assist")

### V5.2.0

[

#### Image Filerobot

Modern easy-to-use image editor for advanced transformations.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/filerobot-image-editor-plugin/ "AI Assist")

### V5.1.0

[

  

#### AI Assist

Bring AI directly into your editor.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/ai-assist-plugin/ "AI Assist")

### V5.0.0

[

  

#### Code Snippet

Insert syntax-highlighted code blocks.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/code-snippet-plugin/ "Code Snippet")[

  

#### Import From Word4

Import a Microsoft Word (.docx) file content to the editor.

](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/import-from-word-plugin/ "Import From Word")

These plugins are included by default if you are using the froala\_editor.pkgd.js file. Otherwise you should include their corresponding stylesheet and JavaScript files. If you have set the **pluginsEnabled** option you should add the corresponding plugin identifier.

  
Sample code:

```
new FroalaEditor('#froala-editor',  { 
  pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'link', 'exportToWord', 'codeSnippet'],
});
```

[Learn more about how Froala plugins works.](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/)

## API Options

In addition to the new plugins’ configurations, the following API options have been added:

V5.5.0

**[headless](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#headless)**

Runs the editor without its own toolbar, popups, or styling, so you can build your own UI and drive the editor through the API.

**[preserveListMarkerStyle](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#preserveListMarkerStyle)**

Controls whether bold or italic on a whole list item is stored on the <li> (styling the marker too) or as <strong> and <em> tags inside it.

**[collabConfig.panel.defaultState](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#collabConfig.panel.defaultState)**

Sets whether the collaborative side panel starts expanded, collapsed, or hidden.

**[aiChatModels](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatModels)** (updated)

Each model’s webSearch and reasoning flags now control the matching AI Chat toggles. An explicit false disables the toggle for that model.

**[aiChatWebSearchEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWebSearchEnabled)** (updated)

Now a request. The toggle stays off when the selected model declares webSearch: false.

**[aiChatReasoningEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatReasoningEnabled)** (updated)

Now a request. The toggle stays off when the selected model declares reasoning: false.

**[aiAssistRequest](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiAssistRequest)** (updated)

The handler receives regenerate: true when the user clicks Try again, so a caching backend can return a fresh answer.

Sets whether the web-search toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off.

**[aiChatModels](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatModels)**

Defines the list of selectable AI models shown in the chat panel’s model dropdown.

**[aiChatDefaultModel](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatDefaultModel)**

Sets which model from aiChatModels is preselected when the panel opens.

**[aiChatReasoningEnabled](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatReasoningEnabled)**

Sets whether the reasoning toggle in the AI Chat panel starts on or off.

**[aiChatStreamResponse](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatStreamResponse)**

**[aiChatSupportedFileTypes](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatSupportedFileTypes)**

Lists the file extensions users can attach as AI Chat context.

**[aiChatMaxFileSizeMB](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFileSizeMB)**

Sets the maximum size, in MB, allowed for a single attached file.

**[aiChatMaxFiles](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatMaxFiles)**

Caps how many files can be attached to one AI Chat conversation.

**[aiChatRequestTimeoutMs](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatRequestTimeoutMs)**

**[aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatIncludeReferenceUrlsInContext)**

**[aiChatPanelWidth](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelWidth)**

**[aiChatPanelMaxWidth](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatPanelMaxWidth)**

**[aiChatWelcomeMessage](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiChatWelcomeMessage)**

**[aiImproveWritingPrompt](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiImproveWritingPrompt)**

The instruction sent to the AI backend whenever Improve Writing runs.

**[selectionActionButtons](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#selectionActionButtons)**

**[inlineSuggestions](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestions)**

**[inlineSuggestionsDelay](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsDelay)**

**[inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#inlineSuggestionsPromptTemplate)**

**[aiSpeechToText](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToText)**

**[aiSpeechToTextWaveform](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextWaveform)**

**[aiSpeechToTextListeningText](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextListeningText)**

**[aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/#aiSpeechToTextMaxDuration)**

## API Events

In addition to the new plugins’ configurations, the following API events have been added:

V5.5.0

[**image.resizeStart**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#image.resizeStart)

Fires when the user grabs an image resize handle, before the size changes.

[**video.resizeStart**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#video.resizeStart)

Fires when the user grabs a video resize handle, before the size changes.

[**video.resizeEnd**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#video.resizeEnd)

Fires when the user releases the video resize handle and the new size is applied.

[**collab.panelStateChanged**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#collab.panelStateChanged)

Fires after the collaborative side panel changes state, passing the new state, the previous state, and what caused it.

[**image.replaced** (updated)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#image.replaced)

Now passes the previous image’s `src` as a third argument, `old_src`.

[**video.replaced** (updated)](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#video.replaced)

Now passes the upload response and the previous video’s `src (old_src)` for both upload and URL replacements.

V5.4.0

[**markdown.beforeGet**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.beforeGet)

Fires before `getMarkdown()` reads the content; returning `false` cancels the read.

[**markdown.afterGet**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.afterGet)

Fires after `getMarkdown()` has retrieved the content.

[**markdown.beforeSet**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.beforeSet)

Fires before `setMarkdown()` applies new content; returning `false` cancels the set.

[**markdown.set**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#markdown.set)

Fires after `setMarkdown()` has successfully applied the content.

[**aiAssist.chatPanelResized**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatPanelResized)

Fires after the user finishes drag-resizing the AI Chat panel.

[**aiAssist.chatBeforeApply**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatBeforeApply)

Fires before a chat response is inserted into the document; returning `false` cancels the insert.

[**aiAssist.chatAfterApply**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.chatAfterApply)

Fires after a chat response has been inserted into the document.

[**aiAssist.improveWritingStarted**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.improveWritingStarted)

Fires when an Improve Writing request is sent to the AI backend.

[**aiAssist.improveWritingResponse**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.improveWritingResponse)

Fires when the AI response for an Improve Writing request is received.

[**aiAssist.reviewStarted**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.reviewStarted)

Fires when a standalone review session opens for AI-suggested changes.

[**aiAssist.hunkResolved**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.hunkResolved)

Fires whenever a single change in the active review session is accepted or rejected.

[**aiAssist.reviewEnded**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.reviewEnded)

Fires when a review session ends because every change has been resolved.

[**aiAssist.beforeHunkInsert**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#aiAssist.beforeHunkInsert)

Fires once per AI-proposed change during a collaborative Suggesting-mode review.

[**dockPanel.opening**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#dockPanel.opening)

Fires when a registered dock panel is about to become visible.

V5.1.0

[**drop.afterCleanup**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#drop.afterCleanup)

This event is triggered just after the clean process during a drop operation.

[**drop.beforeCleanup**](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/#drop.beforeCleanup)

This event is triggered just before the clean process during a drop operation.

 

## Why migrate to V5?

Version 5 offers increased stability and reliability, ensuring a smoother editing experience with fewer disruptions. It also includes a range of new features and bug fixes that enhance functionality and address issues present in previous versions. By upgrading, users can take advantage of these improvements while continuing to enjoy the seamless operation of their favorite editor.

Key improvements:

-   Collaboration features.
-   AI features.
-   Enhanced tables.
-   Improved accessibility.
-   Better iOS mobile support.
-   Enhanced copying and pasting from Word.
-   Headless mode for fully custom editor interfaces.

You can read the [complete changelog here](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/changelog/).

pages.markdown:
# Migrate from Tiptap to Froala This guide maps the Tiptap v3 API to the Froala WYSIWYG Editor v5 API, one topic at a time. Every section pairs your current Tiptap code with the equivalent Froala code so you can move an existing integration over with confidence. ## What you need to know first Tiptap is a headless framework built on ProseMirror. It stores your content as a structured document (a ProseMirror node tree), ships no user interface, and expects you to assemble features from individual extensions and build your own toolbar. Froala takes the opposite approach: it is a batteries-included editor that works directly on HTML, renders a complete toolbar out of the box, and bundles 30+ plugins you switch on with a single option. You move from _assembling an editor_ to _configuring one_. Licensing also differs. Tiptap's core is open source under the MIT license, while advanced Pro extensions require a paid Tiptap Cloud subscription. Froala is a commercial product: you pass a purchased license key through the `key` option. Keep your Froala key handy before you start. Concept Tiptap v3 Froala v5 Initialization `new Editor({ element, extensions })` `new FroalaEditor('#editor', options)` Element targeting A single DOM node via the `element` option CSS selector or DOM node — div, textarea, span, even an img Enabling features Import and add extensions to the `extensions` array 30+ built-in `pluginsEnabled` plugins Toolbar Headless — you build the UI yourself `toolbarButtons` array of button groups Reading content `editor.getHTML()` `editor.html.get()` Writing content `editor.commands.setContent(html)` `editor.html.set(html)` Events `onUpdate`, `onCreate` options `events: { contentChanged: … }` Teardown `editor.destroy()` `editor.destroy()` Licensing MIT core; paid Pro extensions Commercial license key (`key` option) > **The one mental shift:** Tiptap hands you a document model and no UI, so you wire up extensions and render your own buttons. Froala hands you a working editor with a toolbar and plugins already attached, so your job is to choose what to show and set your options. Most of the code you wrote to build Tiptap's interface simply disappears. ## Swap Tiptap for Froala in three steps Remove the Tiptap packages, add Froala, and initialize on the same element. The container's existing HTML becomes your starting content. ### Step 1: Remove Tiptap Uninstall the Tiptap packages and delete the imports and the `useEditor` / `new Editor` setup from your component. ``` # Uninstall the Tiptap packages npm uninstall @tiptap/core @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit @tiptap/extension-image // Delete the Tiptap imports and setup from your component import { useEditor, EditorContent } from '@tiptap/react' import StarterKit from '@tiptap/starter-kit' ``` ### Step 2: Add Froala The quickest path is the CDN. Include the packaged CSS and JS, which bundle the editor and every plugin. ``` // Or install from npm npm install froala-editor ``` ### Step 3: Initialize the editor Both editors mount onto a target element. Tiptap needs an explicit extension list; Froala loads its full feature set automatically, so you only pass your license key. ``` import FroalaEditor from 'froala-editor' // The element's current HTML is used as the initial content const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', }) ``` ## Configuration and options In Tiptap you configure behavior per extension and set editor-wide attributes through `editorProps`. In Froala you set every option in one flat options object. #### Tiptap ``` const editor = new Editor({ extensions: [ StarterKit.configure({ heading: { levels: [1, 2, 3] }, }), ], editable: true, editorProps: { attributes: { class: 'prose focus:outline-none' }, }, }) ``` #### Froala ``` const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { heightMin: 200, heightMax: 400, placeholderText: 'Start typing…', editorClass: 'prose', paragraphFormat: { N: 'Normal', H1: 'Heading 1', H2: 'Heading 2', H3: 'Heading 3', }, }) ``` Froala exposes 240+ options covering sizing, HTML sanitization, paste behavior, and more. Browse the full list in the [Options documentation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/). ## Plugins Tiptap features are extensions you import and add to the array. Froala features are plugins that are already loaded; you narrow them with `pluginsEnabled` or exclude a few with `pluginsDisabled`. #### Tiptap ``` import StarterKit from '@tiptap/starter-kit' import Image from '@tiptap/extension-image' import TextAlign from '@tiptap/extension-text-align' const editor = new Editor({ extensions: [ // Turn off a bundled feature StarterKit.configure({ undoRedo: false }), Image, TextAlign.configure({ types: ['heading', 'paragraph'] }), ], }) ``` #### Froala ``` // Load only the plugins you need const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { pluginsEnabled: ['align', 'image', 'link', 'lists', 'table'], }) // Or load everything and exclude a few const editor2 = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { pluginsDisabled: ['video', 'emoticons'], }) ``` `pluginsDisabled` takes priority over `pluginsEnabled`: a plugin listed in both is disabled. See the complete [plugins list](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/). ## Getting and setting content Both editors read and write HTML. Tiptap can also serialize its document to JSON; Froala works with HTML directly, which usually means less conversion when you persist content. #### Tiptap ``` // Read const html = editor.getHTML() const json = editor.getJSON() // Write (replaces the document) editor.commands.setContent('

New content

') // Insert at the cursor editor.commands.insertContent('inline') ``` #### Froala ``` // Read const html = editor.html.get() // Write (replaces the document) editor.html.set('

New content

') // Insert at the cursor editor.html.insert('inline') ``` ## Events Tiptap accepts event callbacks at the top level of its constructor. Froala groups them under an `events` object, where `this` is the editor instance. Both let you bind and unbind listeners after creation. #### Tiptap ``` const editor = new Editor({ extensions: [StarterKit], onCreate({ editor }) { /* editor is ready */ }, onUpdate({ editor }) { console.log(editor.getHTML()) }, onFocus({ editor }) {}, onBlur({ editor }) {}, }) // Bind / unbind later editor.on('update', () => console.log('changed')) ``` #### Froala ``` const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { events: { initialized() { /* editor is ready; this = editor */ }, contentChanged() { console.log(this.html.get()) }, focus() {}, blur() {}, }, }) // Bind / unbind later editor.events.on('contentChanged', function () { console.log(this.html.get()) }) ``` See the full [events reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/) for the 100+ events Froala fires. ## Methods Tiptap changes state through chained commands and reads state through methods. Froala exposes command methods and namespaced helpers. Note the different read-only calls: Tiptap uses `setEditable`, Froala uses `edit.on` / `edit.off`. #### Tiptap ``` // Formatting via chained commands editor.chain().focus().toggleBold().run() // Read-only mode editor.setEditable(false) // Focus and blur editor.commands.focus() editor.commands.blur() // State checks editor.isActive('bold') editor.isEditable // Teardown editor.destroy() ``` #### Froala ``` // Formatting via command methods editor.commands.bold() // Read-only mode editor.edit.off() editor.edit.on() // Focus and blur editor.events.focus() editor.events.disableBlur() // State checks editor.format.is('bold') // Teardown editor.destroy() ``` Froala ships 220+ methods; browse them in the [methods documentation](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/). ## Image upload This is where the two approaches diverge most. Tiptap's Image extension only renders an image node; you write the upload logic yourself and insert the returned URL. Froala includes a full uploader driven entirely by options. #### Tiptap ``` import Image from '@tiptap/extension-image' const editor = new Editor({ extensions: [StarterKit, Image], }) // You implement the upload and insert the URL yourself async function uploadAndInsert(file) { const body = new FormData() body.append('file', file) const res = await fetch('/upload_image', { method: 'POST', body }) const { link } = await res.json() editor.chain().focus().setImage({ src: link }).run() } ``` #### Froala ``` // Upload, validation, and insertion are built in const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { imageUploadURL: '/upload_image', imageUploadParam: 'file', imageUploadMethod: 'POST', imageMaxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024, imageAllowedTypes: ['jpeg', 'jpg', 'png'], events: { 'image.uploaded'(response) { // Image uploaded to the server }, 'image.error'(error, response) { // Handle upload errors }, }, }) ``` Froala's uploader handles drag-and-drop, paste, progress, and server responses for you. Read the [image upload guide](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/image/upload/) for the full set of parameters and events. ## Framework integration — React Tiptap's React binding gives you the `useEditor` hook and an `` renderer. Froala's `react-froala-wysiwyg` package gives you a single component with two-way binding through `model` and `onModelChange`. #### Tiptap ``` // npm install @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit import { useEditor, EditorContent } from '@tiptap/react' import StarterKit from '@tiptap/starter-kit' function MyEditor() { const editor = useEditor({ extensions: [StarterKit], content: '

Hello World!

', immediatelyRender: false, // avoid SSR hydration errors onUpdate: ({ editor }) => console.log(editor.getHTML()), }) return } ``` #### Froala ``` // npm install react-froala-wysiwyg froala-editor import { useState } from 'react' import 'froala-editor/css/froala_style.min.css' import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css' import FroalaEditorComponent from 'react-froala-wysiwyg' function MyEditor() { const [model, setModel] = useState('

Hello World!

') return ( ) } ``` Froala also provides official SDKs for [Angular](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) and [Vue](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue/) that follow the same `config` / `model` pattern. ## Feature mapping reference Use this table to find the Froala equivalent of the Tiptap extension you rely on today. Where Tiptap requires a separate install, Froala's feature is already present as a plugin. Feature Tiptap v3 Froala v5 Bold / italic / underline StarterKit marks (Bold, Italic, Underline) Built-in `bold`, `italic`, `underline` commands Headings Heading (in StarterKit) `paragraphFormat` option Lists BulletList / OrderedList (in StarterKit) `lists` plugin, `formatUL` / `formatOL` Links Link (in StarterKit) `link` plugin, `insertLink` Images `@tiptap/extension-image` (no upload) `image` plugin (upload built in) Tables `@tiptap/extension-table` (+ related) `table` plugin Text alignment `@tiptap/extension-text-align` `align` plugin Code block CodeBlock (in StarterKit) `codeView` / `codeBeautifier` Placeholder `@tiptap/extension-placeholder` `placeholderText` option Character count `@tiptap/extension-character-count` `charCounter` plugin Undo / redo UndoRedo (in StarterKit) Built-in `undo` / `redo` Markdown Markdown extension `markdown` plugin Toolbar UI None — build your own `toolbarButtons` (built in) ## You're ready to ship You have mapped every core Tiptap API to its Froala equivalent. With the toolbar, plugins, and image uploader already built in, most of your custom UI code can go. Explore these references to fine-tune your setup. [Options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) [Methods](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/) [Events](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/) [Plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/) [Activate license](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/activation/) [React SDK](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/react/) [Angular SDK](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) [Vue SDK](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue/) _Do you think we can improve this article? [Let us know](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/contact/)._

pages.markdown:
# Migrate from Summernote to Froala This guide maps the latest Summernote (jQuery) API onto the Froala WYSIWYG Editor, giving you side-by-side code for every common task — initialization, configuration, plugins, content, events, methods, image upload, and React — so you can switch with confidence. ## What you need to know first Summernote is a jQuery plugin. Every interaction flows through a single overloaded `$(selector).summernote(...)` call: pass an options object to initialize, or pass a command string such as `'code'` or `'destroy'` to invoke a method. It depends on jQuery, and traditionally on Bootstrap, to render its UI. Froala is a standalone ES6 library with no jQuery or Bootstrap dependency. You create an instance with `new FroalaEditor(selector, options)` and call structured, namespaced methods on it directly — for example `editor.html.get()` instead of `$(el).summernote('code')`. Both editors are HTML-first: they read and write HTML strings, so your stored content carries over without a data-model conversion. The other practical difference is licensing. Summernote is MIT-licensed and free. Froala is a commercial product that requires a license `key` passed in the options; you can evaluate it without a key (a small notice appears in the editor). Concept Summernote Froala Initialization `$('#editor').summernote(options)` `new FroalaEditor('#editor', options)` Element targeting jQuery selector on a `div` or `textarea` CSS selector or DOM node — div, textarea, span, even an img Enabling features Pre-bundled in BS3/BS4/BS5/Lite builds 30+ `pluginsEnabled` plugins Toolbar `toolbar` array of `[group, [buttons]]` `toolbarButtons` array of button groups Reading content `$('#editor').summernote('code')` `editor.html.get()` Writing content `$('#editor').summernote('code', html)` `editor.html.set(html)` Events `callbacks: { onChange: … }` `events: { contentChanged: … }` Teardown `$('#editor').summernote('destroy')` `editor.destroy()` Licensing Free, MIT license Commercial license key (`key` option) > **The one mental shift:** stop routing everything through one `$(el).summernote('command', args)` string and start holding the `FroalaEditor` instance you create, then call its namespaced methods directly — `editor.html.get()`, `editor.events.on(...)`, `editor.edit.off()`. The instance _is_ your API. ## Swap Summernote for Froala in three steps Remove the Summernote stack, drop in Froala's single CSS/JS pair, then initialize. Because both editors read the container's existing HTML as their starting content, you usually keep the same markup. ### Step 1 — Remove Summernote Delete the Summernote assets and — if nothing else on the page needs them — the jQuery and Bootstrap dependencies it relied on. Froala needs none of them. ``` ``` ### Step 2 — Add Froala Add the single packaged stylesheet and script. The `.pkgd` build bundles every plugin so you can enable features purely through options. Or install from npm. ``` // Three libraries: jQuery, Bootstrap, Summernote // (plus a build variant per Bootstrap version) ``` ``` ``` ``` npm install froala-editor ``` ### Step 3 — Initialize the editor Summernote initializes through the jQuery plugin and runs inside `$(document).ready`. Froala is a constructor — keep the returned instance, because that object is how you call every method later. Both editors accept a `div` or a `textarea`, and both treat the element's existing HTML as the initial content. Add your commercial `key` in the options. ``` $(document).ready(function () { $('#editor').summernote(); }); ``` ``` const editor = new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY' }); ``` > **No `document.ready` needed:** Froala attaches as soon as the constructor runs, as long as the target element already exists in the DOM. Place the script after the element, or wrap it in a `DOMContentLoaded` listener. ## Configuration and options Both editors take a plain options object. Most Summernote options have a direct Froala counterpart; the names differ but the intent maps cleanly. The toolbar is the biggest structural change: Summernote groups buttons as nested `[groupName, [buttons]]` arrays, while Froala uses a flat `toolbarButtons` array and inserts separators with `'|'`. ### Common options, side by side ``` $('#editor').summernote({ placeholder: 'Write here...', height: 300, focus: true, tabsize: 2, lang: 'en-US', spellCheck: true, toolbar: [ ['style', ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'clear']], ['para', ['ul', 'ol', 'paragraph']], ['insert', ['link', 'picture']] ] }); ``` ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', placeholderText: 'Write here...', heightMin: 300, autofocus: true, tabSpaces: 2, language: 'en_us', spellcheck: true, toolbarButtons: [ 'bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'clearFormatting', '|', 'formatUL', 'formatOL', 'paragraphFormat', '|', 'insertLink', 'insertImage' ] }); ``` ### Option name reference Purpose Summernote Froala Placeholder `placeholder` `placeholderText` Fixed height `height` `heightMin` / `heightMax` Autofocus `focus` `autofocus` Tab size `tabsize` `tabSpaces` Language `lang: 'en-US'` `language: 'en_us'` Spellcheck `spellCheck` `spellcheck` Toolbar `toolbar` (nested groups) `toolbarButtons` (flat, `'|'` separators) Disable drag & drop `disableDragAndDrop` `dragInline` / image drag options Paragraph styles `styleTags` `paragraphFormat` Font names `fontNames` `fontFamily` Browse the full list in the [Froala options reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/). ## Plugins Summernote ships its features baked into each build (BS3, BS4, BS5, Lite) and you opt in by adding the relevant buttons to the toolbar. Froala makes features explicit through the `pluginsEnabled` option. The packaged `.pkgd` build includes every plugin; listing them in `pluginsEnabled` controls which actually load, which keeps the editor lean. ``` // Features are bundled; you surface them // by adding buttons to the toolbar. $('#editor').summernote({ toolbar: [ ['insert', ['link', 'picture', 'video', 'table']] ] }); ``` ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', pluginsEnabled: ['link', 'image', 'video', 'table', 'lists'] }); ``` If you prefer to start from "everything on" and switch a few features off, use the inverse option, `pluginsDisabled`. Anything listed there is excluded while every other bundled plugin stays active. ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', // All bundled plugins load except these: pluginsDisabled: ['video', 'table'] }); ``` > **Tip:** use `pluginsEnabled` for an allow-list (smaller, predictable toolbar) and `pluginsDisabled` for a deny-list (start full-featured, trim a few). See the full catalog in the [plugins reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/). ## Getting and setting content Summernote overloads its `'code'` command: call it with no argument to read HTML, or with a string to write it. Froala splits these into two clearly named methods on the instance, `html.get()` and `html.set()`. Both editors work in HTML, so the value you read from Summernote can be passed straight into Froala. ### Reading the HTML ``` var markup = $('#editor').summernote('code'); ``` ``` const markup = editor.html.get(); ``` ### Writing the HTML ``` $('#editor').summernote('code', '

Hello world

'); ``` ``` // Replace all content editor.html.set('

Hello world

'); // Or insert at the cursor editor.html.insert('inline'); ``` To insert plain text at the cursor — Summernote's `insertText` command — use Froala's `html.insert()` with the text, or the typing API for finer control. ## Events Summernote registers handlers under a `callbacks` object (or via jQuery's `summernote.*` custom events). Froala uses an `events` object with the same shape, and inside every handler `this` is the editor instance — so you can read or mutate content right from the callback. You can also bind later with `editor.events.on(name, handler)`. ### Registering at initialization ``` $('#editor').summernote({ callbacks: { onInit: function () { console.log('Editor ready'); }, onChange: function (contents) { console.log('Changed:', contents); }, onFocus: function () {}, onBlur: function () {} } }); ``` ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', events: { 'initialized': function () { console.log('Editor ready'); }, 'contentChanged': function () { // this is the editor instance console.log('Changed:', this.html.get()); }, 'focus': function () {}, 'blur': function () {} } }); ``` ### Event name reference When Summernote Froala Editor ready `onInit` `initialized` Content changed `onChange` `contentChanged` Gained focus `onFocus` `focus` Lost focus `onBlur` `blur` Key released `onKeyup` `keyup` Key pressed `onKeydown` `keydown` Paste `onPaste` `paste.after` / `paste.before` Image uploaded `onImageUpload` `image.uploaded` / `image.inserted` The full list lives in the [Froala events reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/events/). ## Methods In Summernote, you invoke a method by passing its name as a string to the plugin: `$('#editor').summernote('disable')`. In Froala, you call a namespaced method on the instance you saved at init: `editor.edit.off()`. Holding that instance reference is the key habit to build. ### Frequently used methods Action Summernote Froala Disable editing `summernote('disable')` `editor.edit.off()` Enable editing `summernote('enable')` `editor.edit.on()` Focus `summernote('focus')` `editor.events.focus()` Empty check `summernote('isEmpty')` `editor.core.isEmpty()` Undo `summernote('undo')` `editor.undo()` Redo `summernote('redo')` `editor.redo()` Clear content `summernote('reset')` `editor.html.set('')` Toggle code view `summernote('codeview.toggle')` `editor.codeView.toggle()` Destroy `summernote('destroy')` `editor.destroy()` ### Enable, disable and tear down ``` $('#editor').summernote('disable'); $('#editor').summernote('enable'); $('#editor').summernote('destroy'); ``` ``` editor.edit.off(); editor.edit.on(); editor.destroy(); ``` See every method in the [Froala methods reference](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/methods/). ## Image upload Summernote does not upload by default — it base64-encodes images into the HTML unless you override the `onImageUpload` callback and post the file to your server yourself. Froala makes server upload a first-class feature: point `imageUploadURL` at your endpoint and the editor handles the multipart request, progress, insertion, and error events for you. ``` $('#editor').summernote({ callbacks: { onImageUpload: function (files) { var data = new FormData(); data.append('file', files[0]); $.ajax({ url: '/upload', method: 'POST', data: data, processData: false, contentType: false, success: function (url) { $('#editor').summernote('insertImage', url); } }); } } }); ``` ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { key: 'YOUR_FROALA_LICENSE_KEY', // Editor builds the request and inserts the result imageUploadURL: '/upload', imageUploadMethod: 'POST', imageUploadParam: 'file', events: { 'image.uploaded': function (response) { // response is the raw server response console.log('Uploaded:', response); }, 'image.error': function (error, response) { console.error(error.message); } } }); ``` > **Server response:** Froala expects your endpoint to return JSON containing the uploaded file's link, for example `{ "link": "/uploads/photo.jpg" }`. Froala provides ready-made server SDKs for PHP, Node.js, Java, .NET, Python, and Ruby — see [Uploading images](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/concepts/image/upload/). ## Framework integration — React Summernote has no official React package; teams usually rely on the community `react-summernote` wrapper or hand-roll a jQuery bridge inside `useEffect`. Froala ships an official, maintained component, `react-froala-wysiwyg`, with controlled-value support through `model` and `onModelChange`. ``` npm install react-froala-wysiwyg froala-editor ``` ``` import ReactSummernote from 'react-summernote'; import 'react-summernote/dist/react-summernote.css'; import 'jquery'; import 'bootstrap/js/dist/modal'; function Editor() { return ( ); } ``` ``` import { useState } from 'react'; import FroalaEditorComponent from 'react-froala-wysiwyg'; import 'froala-editor/css/froala_editor.pkgd.min.css'; import 'froala-editor/js/plugins.pkgd.min.js'; function Editor() { const [model, setModel] = useState('

Hello

'); return ( ); } ``` > **Controlled by default:** bind `model` to state and update it in `onModelChange`. Froala also publishes first-party components for [Angular](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/angular/) and [Vue](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/framework-plugins/vue/). ## Feature mapping reference A consolidated cheat sheet for the most common migration tasks. Keep your stored HTML as-is, swap the calls, and add your license key. Task Summernote Froala Initialize `$('#e').summernote(opts)` `new FroalaEditor('#e', opts)` Get HTML `summernote('code')` `editor.html.get()` Set HTML `summernote('code', html)` `editor.html.set(html)` Insert HTML `summernote('pasteHTML', html)` `editor.html.insert(html)` Insert text `summernote('insertText', txt)` `editor.html.insert(txt)` Insert image `summernote('insertImage', url)` `editor.image.insert(url)` Create link `summernote('createLink', {…})` `editor.link.insert(url, text)` Bold `summernote('bold')` `editor.format.toggle('bold')` Foreground color `summernote('foreColor', c)` `editor.colors.text(c)` Focus `summernote('focus')` `editor.events.focus()` Disable / enable `summernote('disable' | 'enable')` `editor.edit.off()` / `editor.edit.on()` Is empty `summernote('isEmpty')` `editor.core.isEmpty()` Code view `summernote('codeview.toggle')` `editor.codeView.toggle()` Undo / redo `summernote('undo' | 'redo')` `editor.undo()` / `editor.redo()` Destroy `summernote('destroy')` `editor.destroy()` Content event `callbacks.onChange` `events.contentChanged` Image upload `callbacks.onImageUpload` `imageUploadURL` option ## You're ready to ship You’ve swapped the library, mapped your options, rewired events and methods, and moved image upload to a real endpoint. From here, lean on Froala’s references to fine-tune the toolbar, plugins, and framework setup. # Migrate Trix Options to Froala Editor ## Options The following guide explains how to pass different Froala Editor options and highlights what to do when migrating from other WYSIWYG editors. ### 1\. Running the code Trix only loads on “trix-editor” elements, Froala uses a DOM selector to fetch the element that includes the editor. In the below example, we are using a div tag that has its id value set to ‘editor’ to get the containing element. Froala Editor. ``` ``` Froala Editor can initialize on more elements than other editors: - Froala can be initiated on an image using the image.min.js plugin ``` ``` - It is possible to initialize the Froala Editor only on a button ``` ``` - It is possible to initialize the Froala Editor on click on an element ```
Hello ContentTools
``` ### 2\. Working with plugins Trix does not use plugins. Froala Editor has over 30 plugins, you can specify required plugins at initialization. **Note:** By default, all plugins are enabled without using the pluginsEnabled option. Also, each plugin requires you to include the corresponding JS and CSS files. Here is the [complete list of plugins](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/plugins/) and the files required by them. Froala Editor ``` new FroalaEditor('#editor', { pluginsEnabled: ['image', 'link'] }); ``` If you do not find the plugin you want, you can create your own. ### 3\. Toolbar Customizations Froala, allows you to choose how to group buttons and choose them based on the screen resolution to properly display the editor on all devices. Please refer to [Options](https://froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/docs/options/) to find a complete list of available options. Froala Editor ``` ``` _Do you think we can improve this article?
